chunks: Our Lord, and make us submit to You, and from our progeny a people submissive to You; show us our rites of worship, and forgive us; indeed, You are the Accepting Repentance, the Merciful.

key_terms.مُسْلِمَيْنِ: Two people submitting (referring to Ibrahim and Ismail)

ai.seo_question: What did Prophet Ibrahim pray for when building the Kaaba?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is viewed as the culmination of Ibrahim and Ismail’s construction of the Kaaba, emphasizing the divine origin of the Hajj rituals (Manasik) and the necessity of repentance even for Prophets. It highlights the concept of 'Ummah' as a cohesive community of submission, linking the physical act of building the Kaaba with the spiritual state of Islam. The invocation underscores Allah’s attribute as Al-Tawwab (The Accepter of Repentance), reinforcing the Shia emphasis on continuous spiritual refinement.
